chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Kurdawayh, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a well into which a drop of blood, or intoxicating nabīdh, or urine, or wine falls. He said: Thirty buckets are to be drawn from it.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.بَوْلٍ: urine as a source of impurity
key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ دَلْوًا: thirty buckets, the specified measure to be drawn
key_terms.خَمْرٍ: wine, an intoxicant and impurity in this context
key_terms.قَطْرَةُ دَمٍ: a drop of blood falling into the well
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: it is to be drawn out, referring to removing water from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if blood, urine, nabīdh, or wine falls into a well?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the purification of a well when certain impure or intoxicating substances fall into it. It specifies that thirty buckets should be drawn from the well, indicating a fiqh ruling related to taharah and water contamination.
